# PipelineScore — Full LLM Documentation Bundle

> Single-fetch context for AI agents. Includes the AGENTS.md guide + the canonical Claude Code skill + the security posture. Apache 2.0. https://pipelinescore.ai

---

## AGENTS.md — How an LLM should invoke PipelineScore

> This is the agent-first entry point. If you're an LLM reading this to decide how to use PipelineScore, this section is for you.

### What PipelineScore does

A standardized 25-task LLM benchmark with a hardware-aware public leaderboard at https://pipelinescore.ai. The user runs a CLI against a local model server (Ollama / LM Studio / MLX / llama.cpp / vLLM) or a frontier API (Anthropic, OpenAI). The score lands on a public board grouped by `(model, hardware_tag)`.

### When to invoke

Use PipelineScore any time the user wants to:
- "Benchmark my Llama on my M3 Max"
- "Score Claude vs GPT on the same tasks"
- "How fast is my RTX 4090 on 70B models?"
- "Test my LoRA / fine-tune / system prompt"
- "Compare model X vs Y on my hardware"

### The one command

```bash
npx @pipelinescore/cli run \
  --provider local \
  --endpoint http://localhost:11434 \
  --model <model-id> \
  --hardware-tag <hardware-tag> \
  --user <user-nickname>
```

For frontier APIs swap `--provider local --endpoint ...` for `--provider anthropic` or `--provider openai`.

### Endpoint defaults by local server

| Server | Port |
|---|---|
| Ollama | http://localhost:11434 |
| LM Studio | http://localhost:1234 |
| llama.cpp server | http://localhost:8080 |
| MLX-Omni / mlx_lm | http://localhost:10240 |
| LiteLLM proxy | http://localhost:8000 |
| vLLM | http://localhost:8000 |

### Hardware tag conventions

Specific, readable strings. Memory bands matter:
- `m3-max-128gb`, `m4-pro-48gb`, `m2-ultra-192gb` (Apple Silicon)
- `rtx-4090-24gb`, `rtx-3090-24gb`, `rtx-3060-12gb` (NVIDIA consumer)
- `a100-80gb`, `h100-80gb`, `h200-141gb` (NVIDIA datacenter)
- `ryzen-7950x-cpu-only`, `ryzen-5950x-rtx-3090` (AMD CPU / mixed)
- `cloud-api` (for frontier API runs)

### Result URL

After the run, the CLI auto-opens `https://pipelinescore.ai/users/<nickname>`. POST THIS URL IN YOUR REPLY too so the user can click it if auto-open didn't fire.

### Three integration paths

1. **MCP tool** — install `@pipelinescore/mcp` from npm, call `run_benchmark`, `get_user_leaderboard`, or `get_user_profile`.
2. **Skill** — `dist/skills/pipelinescore/SKILL.md` for Claude Code / Codex / Cursor.
3. **Direct CLI** — `npx @pipelinescore/cli run ...` from any terminal.

### Anti-patterns to reject

- ❌ Don't fabricate scores. Run the actual CLI.
- ❌ Don't skip `--hardware-tag` on local runs.
- ❌ Don't conflate base + customized models. Use `--config-tag` for LoRA / system prompt / persona variants.
- ❌ Don't promise lab-verified status — that's reserved.
- ❌ Don't ask the user to share their API key with you. The CLI reads it from env locally.

### Rate limits

- 20 submits / IP / hour
- 100 submits / nickname / day
- 5 submits / (nickname, model) / hour

A 429 returns the cooldown duration. Local score is still computed; only the upload is blocked.

### Privacy posture

- API keys are read from the user's env and passed only to the official Anthropic / OpenAI SDK. The PipelineScore backend never sees them.
- Submission transcripts are retained 30 days, then redacted. Score row is permanent.
- All public submissions are visible at the user's profile URL.

### Config tag examples

`system-prompt-coder`, `lora-domain-finance`, `temp-zero`, `tools-enabled`, `rag-prepend`, `cot-style`, `persona-pirate`. Use when the user has customized the model beyond defaults.

---

## What gets scored

Six categories, weighted to mirror real LLM usage:

| Category | Weight | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| Code | 25% | Function-level code generation: Python, JS, SQL, regex |
| Reason | 20% | Multi-step math, logic puzzles, instruction following |
| Write | 15% | Distinct, on-spec prose, summarization |
| Tool use | 15% | API/schema selection, function-call construction |
| RAG | 12% | Grounding, refusal-to-fabricate |
| Speed | 13% | Latency under standardized conditions |

Score is a weighted average (0-100) mapped to one of five tiers:

- **TRUNK** (90-100) — top of the heap
- **MAINLINE** (75-89) — excellent and reliable
- **FEEDER** (60-74) — solid, capable
- **TAP** (40-59) — functional small-branch
- **DRIP** (0-39) — minimal flow

---

## API endpoints (read-only unless noted)

All responses include `api_version: "v1"` field.

| Endpoint | Method | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/leaderboard/users` | GET | Sortable list of all user submissions with hardware tags. Filters: `?provider=`, `?tier=`, `?user=`, `?hardware=`, `?search=`, `?lab_verified=1`, `?sort=score\|date\|user\|model\|provider\|tier`, `?dir=asc\|desc`, `?limit=`, `?offset=` |
| `/v1/leaderboard` | GET | Best-score-per-model leaderboard |
| `/v1/users/{nickname}` | GET | Per-user dashboard: best score, models tried, hardware mix, efficiency aggregates |
| `/v1/users` | GET | User directory (top reviewers) |
| `/v1/beta-testers` | GET | First 50 beta testers list + slots remaining |
| `/v1/models/{slug}` | GET | Per-model stats: median score, recent submissions, top hardware |
| `/v1/compare?a=<slug>&b=<slug>` | GET | Head-to-head model comparison |
| `/v1/testpack` | GET | Daily HMAC-signed 25-task pack |
| `/v1/stats` | GET | Submission count / user count / model count |
| `/v1/submissions` | POST | Submit a benchmark run |
| `/health` | GET | Service health check |

Base URL: `https://api.pipelinescore.ai`

---

## Packages

### `@pipelinescore/cli`
The benchmark runner. `npm install -g @pipelinescore/cli` or `npx @pipelinescore/cli run ...`.

Flags:
- `--provider local|anthropic|openai` (required)
- `--model <id>` (required)
- `--endpoint <url>` (required for `--provider local`)
- `--api-key <key>` (defaults to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` env)
- `--user <nickname>` (alphanum + `. _ -`, 2-40 chars; persisted to `~/.config/pipelinescore/config.json`)
- `--hardware-tag <tag>` (recommended for local; same charset as nickname, 2-60 chars)
- `--config-tag <tag>` (optional; for LoRA / system-prompt / persona differentiation)
- `--backend <url>` (default `https://api.pipelinescore.ai`)
- `--site <url>` (default `https://pipelinescore.ai`)
- `--no-submit` (run benchmark locally without publishing)
- `--no-open` (don't auto-open browser to user's profile)

### `@pipelinescore/mcp`
MCP server. `npm install -g @pipelinescore/mcp` or `npx @pipelinescore/mcp`.

Tools:
- `run_benchmark` — provider, model, user, hardware_tag, config_tag, endpoint, api_key
- `get_user_leaderboard` — provider, tier, user, hardware, lab_verified, sort, dir, limit
- `get_user_profile` — nickname (required)

Install in Claude Code:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pipelinescore": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["@pipelinescore/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Trust boundaries (from SECURITY.md)

- **The npm packages** — published by user `dm797`. Verify provenance with `npm view @pipelinescore/cli` before scripting trust.
- **The backend at api.pipelinescore.ai** — Charles & Roe (Render-hosted, persistent disk, retention policy enforced in code).
- **The frontend at pipelinescore.ai** — Charles & Roe (Cloudflare Workers via OpenNext). Read-only; doesn't accept submissions.
- **Your model server** — you control it.
- **Your API key** — you and the provider (Anthropic / OpenAI). Set a spending cap before benchmarking via frontier.

Vulnerability reports: security@pipelinescore.ai. Don't open a public GitHub issue.
